seeded_payload.research_rationale: EO 9973 (June 28, 1948; 13 FR 3600, read in the held govinfo scan) has one operative provision: it substitutes subdivision (f) of sec. 6.1 of Civil Service Rule VI of EO 9830 (no removal protection for competitive-status holders of Schedule A or B or statutorily excepted positions, except positions the Commission designates as not confidential or policy-determining). The 1989 Codification table (a lead) and the OFR catalog record its revocation by EO 10577 (1954), but an earlier event ended it: EO 10440 sec. 1 (March 31, 1953; 18 FR 1823) amended Rule VI 'as amended by Executive Order No. 9973' to read as a wholly new Rule VI whose sec. 6.1 has no subdivision (f). EO 10440 states no effective date, so the EO 9973 text ended on March 31, 1953. EO 10577 sec. 301 later revoked EO 9973 by name, effective January 23, 1955 (sec. 401), a formal clean-up of an already displaced amendment, recorded as a later event. No savings preserved the EO 9973 text.

savings_residuals.reason: EO 10440 replaced the whole of Rule VI without a savings clause for the text of EO 9973. Its sec. 2 kept positions in Schedules A and B 'as presently constituted' until reclassified; those listings were Commission actions, not provisions of EO 9973. The new sec. 6.4 of EO 10440 kept a similar rule (removal protection for competitive-status incumbents of Schedule A and B positions) by its own force, which is policy continuity, not a survival of EO 9973. The later formal revocation by EO 10577 (effective January 23, 1955) found nothing of EO 9973 still in force.
